 Google’s latest midtier model Gemini 4 Neon is three times faster than Carbon and wins on some metrics 
 by Mike Wheatley 
 After laying low during the summer while competitors Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC unleashed powerful new frontier models, Google LLC is hitting back. 
 Having released its latest flagship model Gemini 4 Carbon one month ago, followed by the cost-effective Gemini 4 Hydrogen, it’s now striking a balance between the two with Gemini 4 Neon. Google announced its latest artificial intelligence offering in a blog post today, saying that Neon is a general-purpose model designed to handle complex coding tasks, multistep agentic workflows and analytical reasoning. 
 Surprisingly, though Carbon is positioned as the company’s strongest model, Neon’s performance surpassed it on some tasks, according to benchmarks the company published today. Google also said Neon completes most tasks about three times as quickly as Carbon at costs of about 60% lower, making it “competitive with the leading models in its class.”
